newsitem.title: USA: Central and South West unit to lower rates.
newsitem.headline: Central and South West unit to lower rates.

text.p: Central and South West Corp said Wednesday that its Central Power and Light Co subsidiary will restore its retail rates to levels existing prior to implementation of the rate increase put into effect under bond in May 1996.
The action is being taken in light of the withdrawal of an order by the Public Utility Commission of Texas immediately reducing CPL's rates to levels outlined in a March 31 final order, it said.
The only two exceptions to the changes are industrial interruptible rates and customer service charges for which the PUCT has indicated they will approve increases requested by CPL.

CPL will begin charging customers at the lowered levels on July 17. Restoring base rates to their pre-bonded levels will decrease the average monthly bill of a residential customer who uses 1,000 kilowatt-hours of electricity per month from about $83.21 to about $78.37.
CPL said it asked the commission to withdraw its order while the rehearing process continues to consider some issues associated with the March 31 final order in the CPL base rate case.
Commissioners, at that time, ordered CPL to lower its retail rates by about $27 million from their pre-bonded levels and by an additional $16 million in 1998 and another $16 million in 1999.
CPL and eight other parties subsequently filed motions for rehearing, and the commission later modified its March 31 final order and agreed to rehear some issues.

CPL said it anticipates that the PUCT will issue a new final order by the end of August incorporating decisions reached during the rehearing process as well as modifications issued on June 20 to the original final order.
Based on CPL's preliminary calculations, the outcome of these decisions could result in a final rate reduction on an annual basis of between $3 million to $25 million.
